sections.title: From mills and workers' huts to a planned district
paragraphs: North of Szent István körút the land was outskirts for most of the nineteenth century, occupied by breweries, mills, a wool-washing works and a poor workers' settlement near the present Vígszínház. The change began with the new boulevard, opened in 1896, which was named for Leopold at the time, and with the Vígszínház, built the same year. The Danube embankment, the Újpesti rakpart, followed between 1900 and 1903, and in 1911 the Palatinus houses, an Art Nouveau group by Emil Vidor, went up on land the Nádor family had received in exchange for Margaret Island.

The real transformation came in the late 1920s. In 1928 the city's public works council decided on a park on the site of a former parquet factory and on a uniform architectural character for the streets around it; a regulation of 1933 fixed the street layout and required perimeter-block building. Almost all buildings in the district date from 1927 to 1944.

sections.title: Modernist blocks and a park for the river
paragraphs: The district is often called Bauhaus, though that is not a precise description, and some blocks, the Dunapark houses in particular, are counted among the best examples of modernist architecture in Hungary. The Phönix house, finished in 1929 by Dávid and Zsigmond Jónás, is an early one. Szent István park was planted in the mid-1930s to plans by Béla Rerrich and took its present name in 1937. It is laid out as a regular pyramid with its wide base on the Danube bank.

The Pozsonyi Road Reformed Church was consecrated in 1940, and the Dunapark café opened in 1938. Hollán Ernő utca has been a pedestrian street since 2009. A large housing estate on Kárpát utca, built between 1976 and 1979, adds a later layer.

sections.title: Wallenberg, the protected houses and memory
paragraphs: In 1944 houses around Szent István körút were placed under the protection of foreign legations, which is why the district is linked with the wartime rescue of Jews. A statue commemorating Raoul Wallenberg in Szent István park was set up in 1949 and removed at night in April of that year, probably on Soviet orders; a replica was erected in 1999. A statue of the philosopher György Lukács in the same park was unveiled in 1985. The poet Miklós Radnóti was a native of the district.

sections.title: Neighbours and the island
paragraphs: Újlipótváros joined District XIII in 1950, together with Margaret Island, which was detached again in 2013. The Margaret Bridge, finished in 1876, is the link to the island and to Buda. Szent István körút separates the district from Lipótváros to the south. Váci út marks its eastern edge, beyond which Angyalföld begins, and north of Dráva utca lies Vizafogó.

highlights: Almost every building dates from between 1927 and 1944.
Szent István park is shaped like a pyramid, wide at the river.
